=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ReferenceDefinitionsAndParagraphs.md === # FEATURE: Reference Definitions and Paragraphs | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Forms paragraphs and collects document-wide link reference definitions. | | Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md | | Provides | link reference definitions, paragraphs | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Form paragraphs from consecutive non-blank lines that are not interpreted as other block types. Collect link reference definitions during block parsing so inline links can resolve definitions anywhere in the document. ## Behavior - Paragraph content is the raw text of its lines, with leading and trailing spaces or tabs removed before inline parsing. A paragraph cannot contain a blank line. - Recognize link reference definitions with up to three spaces of indentation. Definitions may span lines as allowed by CommonMark 0.31.2 and may have an optional title. - Definitions do not render as document content. Collect them across the whole document, including inside block quotes and list items. - Normalize labels by Unicode case folding, trimming surrounding spaces, tabs, and line endings, and collapsing consecutive internal whitespace to one space. - The first definition for a normalized label takes precedence. - A link reference definition cannot interrupt a paragraph. Text that does not form a valid definition remains paragraph content. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC references-and-paragraphs === Intent: The parser passes the complete supplied examples for link reference definitions and paragraphs. Suite: scoped Requires: executable=python3; scope=test Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import os import subprocess import sys pattern = "Link reference definitions|Paragraphs" environment = { **os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join( [os.path.abspath("sources"), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")] ).rstrip(os.pathsep), } result = subprocess.run( [ sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", os.path.abspath("commonmark"), "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", pattern, ], capture_output=True, text=True, env=environment, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC references-and-paragraphs === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the supplied conformance assets unchanged. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation as the parser. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-BlockQuotes.md === # FEATURE: Block Quotes | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark block quotes and their nested block content. | | Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md | | Provides | block quotes | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse block quotes as containers whose contents are parsed using the ordinary block rules. ## Behavior - A block quote marker is `>` optionally preceded by up to three spaces; one following space or tab is part of the marker and is removed from the content. - Consecutive marked lines form a quote. Blank marked lines can occur within it. - Support lazy continuation only for lines that continue an existing paragraph. Do not apply laziness to block starts, code blocks, or other lines that require an explicit quote marker. - Support nested block quotes and all block types inside quotes. - A blank line separates consecutive block quotes. Quotes may interrupt paragraphs. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC block-quotes === Intent: The parser passes the complete supplied examples for block quotes. Suite: scoped Requires: executable=python3; scope=test Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import os import subprocess import sys pattern = "Block quotes" environment = { **os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join( [os.path.abspath("sources"), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")] ).rstrip(os.pathsep), } result = subprocess.run( [ sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", os.path.abspath("commonmark"), "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", pattern, ], capture_output=True, text=True, env=environment, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC block-quotes === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the supplied conformance assets unchanged. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation as the parser. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Lists.md === # FEATURE: Lists | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark bullet and ordered lists, including nesting and tightness. | | Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md | | Provides | list items, lists and tightness | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Parse bullet and ordered list items as containers, including nested blocks and the tight or loose rendering rules defined by CommonMark 0.31.2. ## Behavior - Recognize bullet markers `-`, `+`, and `*`, and ordered markers of one to nine digits followed by `.` or `)`. - Determine item continuation indentation from the marker width and the spaces after it; support the special rules for items beginning with indented code or a blank line. - Support nested lists, lazy paragraph continuation, empty items, and list items containing any supported block type. - Start a new list when list marker types differ. The ordered list start value comes from its first item. - A list is loose when items are separated by blank lines or an item has block children separated by a blank line. Render paragraphs in loose lists with `

` tags and omit those tags for paragraphs in tight lists. Determine tightness independently for nested lists. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC lists === Intent: The parser passes the complete supplied examples for list items and lists. Suite: scoped Requires: executable=python3; scope=test Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import os import subprocess import sys pattern = "List items|Lists" environment = { **os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join( [os.path.abspath("sources"), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")] ).rstrip(os.pathsep), } result = subprocess.run( [ sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", os.path.abspath("commonmark"), "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", pattern, ], capture_output=True, text=True, env=environment, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC lists === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the supplied conformance assets unchanged. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation as the parser. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-EscapesAndCharacterReferences.md === # FEATURE: Escapes and Character References | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses CommonMark backslash escapes and HTML character references. | | Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md | | Provides | backslash escapes, entity and numeric character references | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Interpret backslash escapes and valid HTML entity and numeric character references in inline content according to CommonMark 0.31.2. ## Behavior - A backslash escapes an ASCII punctuation character, rendering that character literally. A backslash before other characters remains literal. - A backslash at the end of an inline line creates a hard line break. - Recognize valid HTML5 named entities with semicolons, decimal references of one to seven digits, and hexadecimal references of one to six digits. - Replace invalid Unicode code points and U+0000 with U+FFFD. - Escape rendered text appropriately for HTML. References and escapes do not create block structure or replace structural Markdown markers. - Do not interpret escapes or references inside code spans, code blocks, autolinks, or raw HTML. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC escapes-and-character-references === Intent: The parser passes the complete supplied examples for backslash escapes and entity and numeric character references. Suite: scoped Requires: executable=python3; scope=test Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import os import subprocess import sys pattern = "Backslash escapes|Entity and numeric character references" environment = { **os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join( [os.path.abspath("sources"), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")] ).rstrip(os.pathsep), } result = subprocess.run( [ sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", os.path.abspath("commonmark"), "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", pattern, ], capture_output=True, text=True, env=environment, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC escapes-and-character-references === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the supplied conformance assets unchanged. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation as the parser. === END ARTIFACT === === BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-CodeSpans.md === # FEATURE: Code Spans | Field | Value | |-------------|-------| | Version | 20261024 V1 | | Description | Parses and renders CommonMark inline code spans. | | Depends On | ARCHITECTURE.md | | Provides | code spans | ## Questions - None. ## Purpose Recognize matching backtick runs in inline content and render their contents as code. ## Behavior - A code span opens with a run of one or more backticks and closes at the next run of exactly the same length. - Convert line endings in code-span contents to spaces. - Remove one leading and trailing space when both are present and the content is not entirely spaces. - Preserve other content literally, including backslashes and character-reference syntax; escape it for HTML without interpreting Markdown inside the span. - If no matching closing run exists, treat the opening backticks as literal text. ## Programmatic Acceptance === AC code-spans === Intent: The parser passes the complete supplied examples for code spans. Suite: scoped Requires: executable=python3; scope=test Probe: --dump-tests Probe Count: json import os import subprocess import sys pattern = "Code spans" environment = { **os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join( [os.path.abspath("sources"), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")] ).rstrip(os.pathsep), } result = subprocess.run( [ sys.executable, "sources/spec_tests.py", "--program", os.path.abspath("commonmark"), "--spec", "sources/spec.txt", "--pattern", pattern, ], capture_output=True, text=True, env=environment, ) print(result.stdout) print(result.stderr, file=sys.stderr) assert result.returncode == 0 === END AC code-spans === ## User Acceptance - None. ## Guardrails - Preserve the supplied conformance assets unchanged. - Do not use a public Markdown implementation as the parser. === END ARTIFACT===
